newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate end up on late speculative spike.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate end up on late speculative spike.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed up 75 basis points on Friday at 20.10 percent on what traders said was speculative spike by big players holding hefty liquidity positions.
Nonetheless, dealers said most of the session had been calm due to the positive impact of benign U.S. producer prices data.
"The data are anticipating inflationary control (in the U.S. economy) and also allowed U.S. long bond yields to fall," a trader said.
U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds had gained 20/32 in late trade to yield 6.73 percent.
Dealers said a firm peso also helped contain speculative pressures on the peso.
"Dollars were patently on offer and that also helped overnight rates to hold steady," the trader added.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contarcts closed 0.7 of a centavo down at 7.9550/7.9580 per dollar.
Overnight rates on bank paper inched up 30 basis points to 20.70 percent.
Banco de Mexico drained a total of 2.130 billion pesos from the market by placing three direct Cetes sales and four repos.
Liquidity of 4.706 billion pesos was due to return to the system on Monday from prior central bank participation.
